The run
is pinned to the environment revision resolved at launch: if the\nenvironment changes in between, the run is rejected with `CONFL

ICT` (409)
rather than executing against a different configuration than the one whose
tools were captured. Use
`GET /projects/{

projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` to see what it
will connect before launching.

When creating a new inline suit
e, `POST .../eval-runs` also accepts `hosts: [{ host: \"Claude\", servers: [\"my-server\"] }]`, using the same host name or ID and
optional server selection as `POST .../eval-suites`. A single host is selected for the run automatically. With multiple attachmen
ts, use `namedHostId` to select the run's client. For an existing suite, update its attachments first. If `hosts` is omitted, the
backend supplies the project's default client.\n\nRun reads and listings expose `client: { id, name, source, hostStyle?, modelId?
}` when recorded. `id` is the named host ID or `null`; `source` is `environment`, `attached_host`, `suite_default`, or `sdk`. The
name is durable even if the host is deleted. SDK executions use `SDK harness`; `launcher.client` separately identifies the launchi
ng process. Older runs without a descriptor omit `client`. `modelSource: \"case\"` means the run's sole model came from its case s
napshot; `client_default` and `override` retain their existing meanings.\n\nEvery run records which environment it used. `GET .../
eval-runs/{runId}` (and\nthe run listings) return `environment: { id, name, revision }` — read from the\nrun's immutable snapshot,

not the suite's current attachments — or `null` for a
run that used a saved server selection.

Per-organization
concurrency i
s capped (default **2** concurrent runs); exceeding it returns\n`429` with `details.reason: \"CONCURRENT_RUN_LIMIT\"` — wait for a

n active run
to finish.

If a server answers `401 OAUTH_REQUIRED`, complete the OAuth flow yourself
(the SDK's `runOAuthLogin`
handles interactive, headless, and\nclient-credentials flows) and upload the token to one of the server's\n[accounts](#server-acc

ounts). Subsequent runs inject the stored token, and
refresh it server-side when you stored a refresh token.

## Reasoning effo

rt

A reasoning effort is a **saved setting on a model selection**, not a free-standing
field. A `ModelSelection` (`modelId`, `
source`, an optional `connectionRef`, and a\n`fallback`) carries it as `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the same shape is\naccepted

everywhere a model choice is saved:

| Where | Field |
| - | - |
| Client (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`) |
`set.modelSelection` (or `config.modelSelection` on a whole-config replacement) |\n| Project environment (`POST`, `PATCH`, `POST .
../ensure-adhoc`) | `modelSelection`, read back on the environment |\n| Eval case (`POST`, `PATCH .../cases`) | `models[].selectio
n`, read back on the case |\n| Eval suite (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}`) | `executionConfig.modelSelection`

``

* **Levels.** `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Which of
 them a model accepts is `supportedReas
oningEfforts` on each row of the public\n `GET /v1/models` catalog. An empty or absent list means no effort is offered for\n tha
t model — do not guess one.\n* **Applied or refused, never dropped.** A saved effort is applied by the route\n the run takes and
recorded on the execution record, or refused with\n `capability_missing` before any spend. An effort replaces the sampling\n tem
perature.\n* **A selection belongs to one model.** It must be for the `model` / `modelId` it\n sits beside (`400` otherwise); sen
t alone it pins its own model. A bare model\n change on a suite or environment drops a selection saved for the old model\n inste
ad of failing.\n* **Cases keep their selections.** A `models` PATCH replaces the array, but an\n entry that omits `selection` kee
ps the case's existing selection for that\n model. Send `selection: null` to drop it.\n* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved sele
ction on a client `set`, an environment\n or a suite, keeping the bare model id.\n* **Never a secret.** A selection has no creden
tial field; an unknown key\n (`apiKey`, …) is a `400`.\n* **Environments need the capability.** `GET .../environments/capabilitie
s`\n reports `modelSelections`; an older deployment rejects the field.\n* **`advancedConfig.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was
never applied, so\n writing it is a `400` pointing at `models[].selection.settings`, and a stored\n value is refused by the run

ner.

`POST /chat-sessions/messages` takes a top-level `reasoningEffort` for a
per-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pi
nned on the session's **first\nturn** (a continuation that restates it is refused), it wins over the effort a\n`hostId`'s saved se
lection carries, and it cannot be combined with `temperature`.\n\nThe SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the same
operations:\n`--effort` / `reasoningEffort` is a shorthand that edits the selection the target\nalready has, and is refused (`sen

d modelSelection`) when there is none.

## Not in the API yet

To set expectations while in preview, these are **not** availab

le over the API
today (most exist in the hosted inspector UI):

* Creating or revoking API keys (UI-only by design — see [Authe
ntication](#authentication))\n* Chat and conformance suites\n* Browser-based OAuth flows initiated by the API (complete OAuth your

self,
 then upload the token to one of the server's [accounts](#server-accounts))

If one of these blocks you, tell us on
[Di

scord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) — it directly shapes what we
stabilize first.

## Versioning & stability

* The API is
**path-versioned** (`/api/v1`). When it reaches general\n availability, breaking changes will require a new version path.\n* **Du
ring the preview**, breaking changes to v1 may still happen; we'll note\n them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changel
og/overview.md).\n* **Additive changes** — new endpoints, new optional request fields, new\n response fields, new error codes — a
re considered non-breaking and can ship\n at any time. Write clients that ignore unknown fields.\n* Error **codes** are stable id

entifiers; error **messages** are not.

### Renamed surfaces

Three nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `
scenario` is\n**study**, `journey` is **goal**, and `wave` is **swarm run**. The paths, the\noperation names, the SDK types and th

e noun-bearing response fields all moved:

| Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/proje
cts/{projectId}/studies[/{studyId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/s
tudies/{studyId}/…` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study`
|\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys[/{journeyId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey
-runs/{runId}` | `/projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings`
| `.../goals-overview`, `.../goal-findings` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-ru

ns/{swarmRunId}/insights` |

Response fields followed their nouns: `scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →
`goalId`, `waveId` →

`swarmRunId`, and `sessionsPerTarget` → `iterations`.

Two reads became one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and
`get_user_testing_scenario` served the environment id and the insights\nenvelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-dep

endent fields are
absent rather than null when you may not have them.

**Every old path still works** and is unchanged, includi
ng its old response\nspellings. Each one answers with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` header naming\nits successor. They are undo
